subject: Catalyst: request for early termination pathway and downgrade safeguards

Cc: legal@catalysthealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: early termination path & downgrade protections

Hi Kim,

Thanks for taking this. We had a last-minute budget committee meeting and Catalyst needs a path to materially reduce committed capacity for the remainder of FY26 — this is not a termination for cause, it's a business-led downsizing.

What we need from Redwood: a clear, contract-amendable early termination / staged downgrade option that preserves a fallback for production continuity (we can't lose inference during the month-over-month reduction), plus limited credit or bridge support to smooth the transition. Specifically: 
- Ability to step down committed GPU capacity over a 12-week ramp (milestone schedule provided in attached SOW).
- An explicit ‘downgrade protection’ so production traffic falls back to a lower committed tier rather than immediate overage.
- A one-time bridge credit to offset the remaining committed spend if we accelerate the ramp before week 6.

We appreciate Redwood's partnership here — Catalyst is an early adopter and we'd like to make this a documented exception rather than an immediate contract break. Attached is the SOW (v3) and our usage snapshot for the last 60 days. Legal is copied for formality.

Can your team propose a concrete amendment and confirm whether this requires senior exec sign-off?

Best,
Elena Torres
Director, Partnerships — Catalyst Health
Elena Torres | catalysthealth.com

Attachment: usage_report_May2026.csv (CSV, 34KB)

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: early termination path & downgrade protections

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the SOW + usage. We can support a staged downgrade workflow with guardrails; however the bridge credit you're requesting exceeds the standard deal-desk thresholds and will need exec clearance.

Proposal (draft amendment highlights):
- 90-day staged ramp divided into three 30-day phases with target committed capacity reductions of 40% / 30% / 30%.
- During the ramp, we will route traffic to a reserved lower-tier pool to avoid immediate overage (Downgrade Protection).
- One-time bridge credit equal to 30% of the unrun committed spend if Catalyst elects to accelerate the ramp before day 45. Credit applied as a prepaid credit on the account over the following billing cycle.
- Opt-out carve: Catalyst may terminate remaining commitments for cause at any time; non-for-cause accelerated termination requires the staged ramp or acceptance of the bridge credit calculus above.

Next steps I propose:
1) We prepare an amendment document (I attached a redline draft).
2) I escalate for exec approval given the non-standard credit; will need yes/no from Deal Desk Director or VP of Sales (see Marissa & Aditya on cc).
3) If approved, we send the amendment + DocuSign link to Elena and legal for signature.

If this sounds reasonable, Marissa / Aditya — can you review the approach and confirm recommended credit ceiling? I'll escalate to leadership if we align.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Director — Redwood Inference

Kim / Aditya — quick internal note. I reviewed the usage file and revenue profile. Catalyst is a strategic mid-market reference; preserving relationship is high priority. A couple of suggested guardrails before we push to exec: 
- Keep the bridge credit at 30% of unrun committed spend but cap the absolute credit at $150k exposure. That keeps the finance hit bounded.
- Approve the 90-day phased ramp but add a minimum commitment floor of 25% of original capacity to avoid complete churn risk.
- Require that Catalyst schedule a weekly cadence with our CS team during the ramp (operational acceptance) — helps catch regressions and avoid SLA thrashing.

If Kim thinks the $150k cap and 25% floor are acceptable to Catalyst, I recommend we escalate to Rishi for sign-off with those limits.
